title: Chermoula Salmon
subtitle: Moroccan herb and spice-marinated salmon baked in the oven
excerpt: Chermoula is a Moroccan marinade of fresh coriander, parsley, garlic, cumin, and lemon. It works particularly well with salmon: the herbs char slightly in the hot oven while the fish stays moist inside. The marinade takes 5 minutes to make and the fish needs just 15 minutes to cook.
sourceNotes: Based on the classic North African chermoula used across Morocco and Algeria. The marinade is traditionally used with fish and is well-suited to salmon.

content.text: Marinate the salmon for at least 10 minutes at room temperature before grilling. This gives the spices time to start penetrating the flesh and means the fish cooks more evenly.
Make the chermoula. Finely chop the coriander and parsley. Mix with the garlic, cumin, both paprikas, turmeric, chilli flakes, lemon juice, and olive oil. Season with salt and stir well.

Place the salmon fillets on a lined baking tray. Spoon the chermoula generously over each piece, coating the top and sides. Leave to marinate for 10 minutes at room temperature while the grill heats up.
Heat the oven grill to high. Grill the salmon for 12 to 15 minutes until the chermoula is slightly charred and the fish flakes easily with a fork. The centre should still be a little pink.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges, couscous, and a simple salad.

items.symptom: Chermoula burns before the fish is cooked.
items.cause: Tray too close to the grill element.
items.fix: Move the tray one shelf lower and reduce grill heat.

items.cause: Left under the grill too long.
items.fix: Check at 10 minutes. Done when it flakes easily.

items.symptom: Marinade is too thick to spread.
items.fix: Add another tbsp of olive oil and stir again.
